 Elle and Dakota Fanning to share the big screen for the first time in movie adaptation of hit book 
 By Bryony Jewell 
 on 17th November 2026 in Celebrity 
 By Bryony Jewell 
 on 17th November 2026 in Celebrity 
 Share
 Readers, get ready, as the countdown is well and truly on for the adaptation of one of BookTok’s most buzzy books of recent years.
 Truthfully, most of Kristin Hannah’s reads have found themselves going viral , but perhaps The Nightingale is the biggest of them all.
 Today's top videos
 Fans love the historical read, which follows two sisters during World War II, and it’ll soon be brought to life on the big screen by two real-life sisters.
 Elle and Dakota Fanning will share the big screen in The Nightingale movie. Pic: The Nightingale / Instagram 
 Elle and Dakota Fanning have been cast to play the leads, Isabelle Rossignol and Vianne, and this will be the first time they’ve worked together.
 Although their casting was confirmed earlier in 2026, it’s taken until November for us to have a first look at them in action as their characters.
 On Monday, the sisters attended a fan event to reveal the book tie-in cover for the movie, ahead of the trailer being released on Thursday.
 The Nightingale by Kristin Hannah. Pic: Amazon 
 Photos and videos show them posing with the book, which features their faces on either side of the cover, and posing in coordinated midi skirts and shirts.
 Kristin Hannah fans were delighted to see the cover reveal, with one person saying: ‘I’m soooo ready but also completely aware I’ll never recover from this.’
 ‘I am SO excited for this!! Been waiting for a movie since I read the book in 2015,’ added another, while a third said: ‘Can’t wait to cry in the theatre watching this.’
 Dakota previously spoke about working with her sister on the project while on Josh Horowitz’s Happy, Sad, Confused podcast.
 Elle and Dakota Fanning will share the big screen in The Nightingale movie. Pic: The Nightingale / Instagram 
 She said: ‘I think Elle and I were nervous, like we didn’t want to admit how nervous about it we were because it was that little intrusive thought of, “Is this going to be okay? Are we going to be able to do this? Is it going to be weird? Are we going to be laughing? What is it going to be like?”
 ‘I don’t think we wanted to talk about it too much because it was sort of that thing of like "I think it’ll be fine”. Scheduling-wise, things were really complicated, but it was really important to us that we started the movie together to just see right away, and the first day couldn’t have been more normal, or easier.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Nightingale (@nightingalemovie) 
 ‘I was like, “Oh, it’s because we spent our whole childhoods playing together and making up these scenarios" 
 'That’s how we learned how to act, with each other, in our playroom, making up the craziest stuff.'
